## Pull request overview

Fixes several console/runtime regressions around form schema fetching, MSW mock initialization, and non-grid view layout sizing, plus adds targeted regression coverage and test/build config updates.

**Changes:**
- Update `ObjectForm` to handle falsy schema fetch results and clear loading on schema-fetch errors.
- Prevent duplicate manifest data seeding in the console MSW browser mock startup.
- Fix `ObjectView` height/scroll chain for non-grid view types and add Vitest aliases + regression tests.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `vitest.config.mts` | Adds missing module aliases needed for tests to resolve subpath/package imports. |
| `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` | Enforces a flex column + height chain and wraps content to allow non-grid views to render/scroll correctly. |
| `packages/plugin-form/src/ObjectForm.tsx` | Improves schema-fetch failure handling to avoid infinite loading and adds an early loading-clear fallback. |
| `apps/console/src/mocks/browser.ts` | Removes redundant manifest seeding to avoid duplicating records in browser MSW mode. |
| `apps/console/src/__tests__/ConsoleIssues.test.tsx` | Adds regression tests covering form loading, initial data fetch, and non-grid view rendering paths. |
</details>

## Unused variable, import, function or class

Unused imports fireEvent, within.

[Show more details](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/security/code-scanning/400)

This test currently only asserts that the loading indicator disappears when `dataSource` is missing. Given the form can’t function without a DataSource (and the component has a specific error UI), it would be stronger and less prone to false positives to assert the error state/message is rendered (e.g., “Error loading form” / “DataSource is required …”) rather than just “not loading”.

`createMockDataSource()` ends with `} as DataSource`, which disables compile-time checking of the mock’s method signatures (e.g. `delete` should take `(resource, id)` per `DataSource`). Consider using `satisfies DataSource` (or `const base: DataSource = { ... }`) so signature mismatches are caught by TypeScript, and only use a targeted cast in the one test that intentionally returns `null` from `getObjectSchema`.
